# Action tools for agents: cancel_run and resume_run

## What to build

Two graph-manager MCP tools (KAN-91 #5, #9) that let an agent in a graph-manager terminal stop and resume runs of its own workspace, in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/`, registered in `TOOLS` (`tools/index.ts`):

- `cancel_run { runId }`: when the run's page is live, `POST <page>/abort` through the same access graph-manager's run-page proxy uses (`livePage(runDir)` gives the URL, and for a sandboxed run the upstream address and token). When that page does not answer and the run is sandboxed with a record, `ctx.sandboxes.stop(ws.id, runId)`. Otherwise the tool error `run <id> is not running (<status>)`. Success: `Stopped run <id>. Resume it with resume_run.` Same effect as Ctrl+C or the UI's abort: worktrees and state are kept.
- `resume_run { runId }`: calls the existing `resumeRun(ctx, ws, runId)` (`routes/resume.ts:35-89`). A `SandboxError` becomes a tool error with its message (and output tail). On success the calling terminal becomes the run's origin: `ctx.runOrigins.set(ws.id, runId, tc.terminal.id)`, and the text is `Resumed run <id>. You'll get its events in this terminal.`

Already delivered by dependency tasks (read these files first):
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/run-origins.ts`: `export class RunOrigins { set(wsId, runId, terminalId): void; get(wsId, runId): string | undefined; delete(wsId, runId): void; entries(): { wsId: string; runId: string; terminalId: string }[] }`, and `AppContext.runOrigins: RunOrigins` (`app.ts`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/run-helpers.ts`: `requireWorkspace(tc)`, `isToolResult(v)`, `runDirOrError(ws, runId)` (error `unknown run <id>`), `readTailLines`, `fenced(text)`, and more.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/tool-test-helpers.ts`: `toolApp(overrides?)` (app with internal token `t0ken`, git workspace `wsDir`, `terminalId`, `rootTerminalId`, `call(name, input, opts?)`, `config`, `cleanup()`), `writeRun(wsDir, runId, overrides?)` (valid `state.json`, default status `failed`).
- `tools/index.ts` already lists `open_start_run`, `list_runs`, `get_run_log`, `list_graphs`, `get_node_output`, `get_artifacts`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts` — `LivePage` (lines 111-119: `url`, `pid`, optional `upstream { host, port, hostPort?, token? }`), `livePage(runDir)` (157-161), `runDetail` (485-515; `summary.status` is `interrupted` for a `running` state with no live process), `runDirOf` (518).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.ts` — `WEB_TOKEN_HEADER` (line 9), `upstreamPort(url)` (24-34), `upstreamGetJson(target, pathname, timeoutMs)` (37-65: the Host header must be `127.0.0.1:<hostPort ?? port>`, token in `x-graph-execution-token`), and how the proxy picks its target (86-99): `web?.upstream ?? { host: "127.0.0.1", port: upstreamPort(web.url) }`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/web/server.ts` (lines 219-223 and 520-531) — `POST /abort` answers 200 `{ ok: true }`, or 409 `{ error: "the run has ended" }` once the run ended; every request must have Host `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`, the token when the page has one, and a non-GET request with an `Origin` header other than the page's own is refused (send no Origin).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` (lines 481-484 `recordOf(wsId, runId)`, 686-692 `stop(wsId, runId): Promise<boolean>`, false without a record).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/resume.ts` (lines 31-89 `resumeRun`, 91-109 the route's `SandboxError` handling, 111-117 the Stop sandbox route).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts` (lines 10-19) — `SandboxError(status, message, output?)`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` (line 53) — `lastLines(text, n)`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.test.ts` (lines 22-63) — a fake run page server (`http.createServer`, checks Host, answers `POST /abort`) and a `web.json` `{ url: "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/", pid: process.pid }` in the run folder that makes the run live.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runoptions.test.ts` (lines 10-34) — a fake engine bin (`fake-ge.mjs` that records its argv and exits 0) passed as `graphExecutionBin`.
- `docs/prd/agent-supervisor.md` — table rows `cancel_run`, `resume_run`; Decisions rows on cancel_run/resume_run.

## Patterns to follow

**Upstream request** (`proxy.ts:37-65`, to mirror for POST):
```ts
const headers: OutgoingHttpHeaders = { host: `127.0.0.1:${target.hostPort ?? target.port}`, accept: "application/json" };
if (target.token) headers[WEB_TOKEN_HEADER] = target.token;
const req = http.request({ host: target.host, port: target.port, method: "GET", path: pathname, headers }, (res) => { … });
req.setTimeout(timeoutMs, () => req.destroy(new Error(`${pathname} timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms`)));
```

**SandboxError to a reply** (`routes/resume.ts:99-105`):
```ts
if (err instanceof SandboxError) {
  … error: err.message, …(err.output ? { output: lastLines(err.output, 20) } : {})
}
```

**Tool start** (helpers from run-helpers.ts):
```ts
const ws = requireWorkspace(tc);
if (isToolResult(ws)) return ws;
const runDir = await runDirOrError(ws, i.runId);
if (typeof runDir !== "string") return runDir;
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export function upstreamPost(target: { host: string; port: number; hostPort?: number; token?: string }, pathname: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<{ status: number; body: string }>` next to `upstreamGetJson`: same headers (Host, token, no Origin), method POST, `content-length: 0`, resolves with the status code and body text for ANY status, rejects on a network error or the timeout.
- **VALIDATE**: `cd apps/graph-manager && npx vitest run src/server/proxy.test.ts` (add one case there: `upstreamPost` to the fake upstream's `/abort` resolves `{ status: 200 }`).

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/cancel-run.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export const cancelRunTool = defineTool({ name: "cancel_run", input: z.object({ runId: z.string().min(1).describe("The run id") }), … })`, description e.g. "Stop a running graph-execution run of this workspace, like Ctrl+C or Abort in the UI. Its worktrees and state are kept, so resume_run can continue it."
  1. workspace + run folder.
  2. `const status = async () => (await runDetail(ws, runId))?.summary.status ?? "unknown";`
  3. A suite folder (`existsSync(path.join(runDir, SUITE_FILE))`, `SUITE_FILE` from `graph-execution/api`) → error `run <id> is a suite; cancel suites from their terminal`.
  4. `const page = await livePage(runDir)`. Target: `page.upstream ?? { host: "127.0.0.1", port: upstreamPort(page.url) }` (no port → treat as no page).
  5. With a target: `upstreamPost(target, "/abort", 5000)`:
     - 200 → `{ text: `Stopped run ${runId}. Resume it with resume_run.` }`
     - 409 → `{ isError: true, text: `run ${runId} is not running (${await status()})` }`
     - another status → `{ isError: true, text: `the page of run ${runId} answered ${status}` }`
     - rejected (no answer): if `tc.ctx.sandboxes?.recordOf(ws.id, runId)` → `await tc.ctx.sandboxes.stop(ws.id, runId)` and the success text; else `{ isError: true, text: `could not reach the page of run ${runId}: ${err.message}` }`.
  6. No page → `{ isError: true, text: `run ${runId} is not running (${await status()})` }` (e.g. `applied`, `failed`, `interrupted`).
- **IMPORTS**: `existsSync` from `node:fs`; `path`; `SUITE_FILE` from `graph-execution/api`; `livePage, runDetail` from `../runs.js`; `upstreamPost, upstreamPort` from `../proxy.js`; helpers from `./run-helpers.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: the page's `/abort` returns 409 once the run has ended but its page is still open (it waits for `POST /close`): that is "not running", not a failure of the tool. Do not delete or edit anything in the run folder.
- **VALIDATE**: `cd apps/graph-manager && npx vitest run src/server/tools/cancel-run.test.ts`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/resume-run.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `export const resumeRunTool = defineTool({ name: "resume_run", input: z.object({ runId: z.string().min(1).describe("The run id of a failed, aborted or interrupted run") }), … })`, description e.g. "Resume a failed, aborted or interrupted run of this workspace from where it stopped (graph-execution --resume). Commit your fix first: resume refuses when the task files, spec or config changed. You become the run's origin and get its events in this terminal."
  1. workspace + run folder.
  2. `await resumeRun(tc.ctx, ws, runId)` (from `../routes/resume.js`); catch `SandboxError` → `{ isError: true, text: err.output ? `${err.message}\n\n${fenced(lastLines(err.output, 20))}` : err.message }` (when `message` already equals the output tail, as `resumeRun` does for a failed engine start, print it once). Rethrow other errors (the route turns them into `isError`).
  3. On success: `tc.ctx.runOrigins.set(ws.id, runId, tc.terminal.id)`; return `{ text: `Resumed run ${runId}. You'll get its events in this terminal.` }`.
- **GOTCHA**: `resumeRun` already refuses suites (`suites are resumed from a terminal`), a live run (`the run is live`), a finished one (`the run already finished (applied)`), and an unreadable state (`unknown run`); keep its messages. It starts the engine detached with `--resume --run <id> --web` (non-sandbox) or a new container (sandbox). Record the origin only after it succeeded.
- **VALIDATE**: `cd apps/graph-manager && npx vitest run src/server/tools/resume-run.test.ts`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/index.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: append `cancelRunTool as GmTool, resumeRunTool as GmTool` to `TOOLS`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/cancel-run.test.ts`

Inside `describe.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`, with `toolApp()` and `writeRun()`:
- live run: start a fake page server (copy `proxy.test.ts:22-45`, `listen(0, "127.0.0.1")`) whose `POST /abort` answers 200 `{ ok: true }` and records the request (method, Host header, absence of `origin`); `writeRun(wsDir, id, { status: "running" })` and `web.json` `{ url: "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/", pid: process.pid }` → text `Stopped run <id>. Resume it with resume_run.`; the fake saw `POST /abort` with Host `127.0.0.1:<port>`. To also check the "status becomes aborted" criterion, make the fake's `/abort` handler rewrite `state.json` with `status: "aborted"` (what the engine does) and then assert `list_runs` shows `aborted`.
- the fake answers 409 → `run <id> is not running (…)` (isError).
- finished run (`writeRun(..., { status: "applied" })`, no web.json) → `{ isError: true, text: "run <id> is not running (applied)" }`.
- unknown run id → `unknown run <id>`; a terminal outside workspaces (`rootTerminalId`, cwd `config.workspacesDir`) → `this terminal is not inside a graph-manager workspace`.
- close the fake server in `afterEach` (`closeAllConnections()` then `close()`).

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/resume-run.test.ts`

- Through the API (with `toolApp({ graphExecutionBin: fakeBin })`, the fake bin from `runoptions.test.ts:10-13` writing `argv.json` and exiting 0): aborted run → text `Resumed run <id>. You'll get its events in this terminal.`, argv.json contains `["--resume", "--run", "<id>", "--web"]`. Applied run → isError `the run already finished (applied)`. Unknown id / outside workspace errors as above. A fake bin that prints `boom` and exits 1 → isError text containing `boom`.
- Origin recorded: `AppContext` is not reachable through `buildApp`, so call the tool directly: `await resumeRunTool.run({ runId }, { ctx: { config: testConfig(dir, { graphExecutionBin: fakeBin }), runOrigins: new RunOrigins(), sandboxes: undefined } as unknown as AppContext, terminal: { id: "t9", title: "t", cwd: wsDir, status: "idle", createdAt: "x" } as TerminalInfo, workspace: resolveWorkspace(workspacesDir, "github~octo~hello")!, cwd: wsDir })` and assert `ctx.runOrigins.get("github~octo~hello", runId) === "t9"`; for an applied run the origin stays unset.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/internal/tools` lists `cancel_run` and `resume_run`.
- [ ] `cancel_run` on a live run sends `POST /abort` to its page (Host `127.0.0.1:<port>`, page token for a sandboxed run, no Origin) and returns `Stopped run <id>. Resume it with resume_run.`; its status becomes `aborted` (engine behaviour, simulated by the fake page in the test).
- [ ] `cancel_run` on a sandboxed run whose page does not answer calls `ctx.sandboxes.stop`; on a finished run it returns `run <id> is not running (applied)`.
- [ ] `resume_run` on an aborted run starts it again via `resumeRun` and the caller becomes its origin (`ctx.runOrigins.get(ws.id, runId) === terminal id`); a `SandboxError` is returned as a tool error with its message.
- [ ] Both tools return `this terminal is not inside a graph-manager workspace` outside a workspace and `unknown run <id>` for a bad or foreign run id.
- [ ] Tests pass: `cd apps/graph-manager && npx vitest run src/server/tools src/server/proxy.test.ts`

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
cd apps/graph-manager && npx vitest run src/server/tools src/server/proxy.test.ts src/server/routes/resume.test.ts
```
